Sunlight contains all colors of the visible spectrum, but as it enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules and scatters in all directions. Shorter wavelengths of light, like blue and violet, scatter much more strongly than longer wavelengths like red and yellow—a phenomenon known as Rayleigh scattering. Although violet scatters even more than blue, our eyes are more sensitive to blue and some violet is absorbed in the upper atmosphere, so we perceive the sky as blue.
